newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Berjaya unit to lead in CAP restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Berjaya unit to lead in CAP restructuring.

text.p: Berjaya Lottery Management (HK) Ltd is taking the lead in restructuring Central Azucarera de Pilar (CAP) under a swap agreement, documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Tuesday said.
The SEC is set to consider the proposal on Thursday.
Berjaya Lottery is a member of Malaysia's Berjaya Group Bhd.

Based on the proposal, Berjaya will exchange its 40 percent stake in Philippine Gaming and Management Corp (PGMC) for a 54.3 percent stake in CAP, making it the biggest shareholding group in the sugar company-turned-gaming corporation.
CAP, in turn, will own 100 percent of PGMC.
PGMC will assume and equitise CAP's debt worth 105.8 million pesos, while CAP will exchange 52 million of its shares for 250,000 PGMC shares, or 100 percent of the gaming company.
CAP will also assume PGMC's liabilities in exchange of an additional 32.9 million CAP shares.
PGMC owns the equipment leased by the state-owned Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office which runs a lottery on the main island of Luzon.
Minority shareholders of PGMC, including First Abacus Financial Holdings Corp, will collectively own 31.5 percent of CAP.
Former majority owners of CAP, Beckford Trade & Finance Ltd and Premier Equity Ltd, will reduce their stakes to 13.4 percnet and 0.8 percent respectively.
CAP is projecting a steady growth in its net income after taking over the operations of PGMC, saying income will rise to 38.76 million pesos next year from 14.45 million pesos this year.
